key_developments.event: Norbert of Xanten founds Prémontré in the diocese of Laon.
Honorius II confirms the order; Norbert becomes Archbishop of Magdeburg.
Premonstratensians prominent in the Wendish Crusade missions east of the Elbe.
Innocent IV reaffirms the order's privileges and exempt status.

_quarry.description: The Norbertines, a reformed order of canons regular following the Rule of Saint Augustine, were founded by Norbert of Xanten at Prémontré in Picardy in 1120. Unlike the Cistercians' lay-monastic model, the Premonstratensians combined the active pastoral work of canons (preaching, parish ministry, missions to recently-converted lands) with monastic discipline. The order expanded rapidly across the Empire and into Slavic missionary territories; by 1250 there were roughly 600 houses, many active in the Wendish missions of the 12th century.
